trial_court: Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sirmaur, District Nahan, H.P.
case_name: Neha Sharma & Others vs Ms. Rajani Devi & Another
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Marriage between respondent No.1 and respondent No.3 was solemnized on 13th May, 2013. Respondent No.1 filed a complaint under Section 12 of the Protection of Women under Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against petitioners as well as respondent No.3. Interim maintenance of Rs.7000/- per month was granted in favour of respondents No.1 and 2.

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash criminal proceedings under Section 482 of the Code is to be exercised sparingly and with caution.
legal_principles.held: No doubt, under Section 482 of the Code, the High Court has inherent power to quash the criminal proceedings even in those cases which are not compoundable, where the parties have settled the matter between themselves.

legal_principles.principle: The guiding factor in quashing criminal proceedings is to secure the ends of justice or prevent abuse of the process of any Court.
legal_principles.held: When the parties have reached the settlement and on that basis petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding factor in such cases would be to secure: (i) ends of justice, or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

legal_principles.principle: Criminal cases involving heinous and serious offences, such as murder, rape, or dacoity, should not be quashed merely on the basis of a settlement between the parties.
legal_principles.held: Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society. Similarly, for offences alleged to have been committed under special statute like the Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by Public Servants while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender.

legal_principles.principle: Criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or family disputes, should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.
legal_principles.held: On the other, those criminal cases having overwhelmingly and pre-dominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.

outcome.final_order: Prayer has been made on behalf of the petitioners for quashing of complaint dated 13.10.2015 filed under Section 12 of the Protection of Women under Domestic Violence Act, 2005.
